A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that isolation on average can be a powerful technique in the analysis of noisy hashing schemes.
we provide a new tool, isolation on average, to design Fourier sampling algorithms for a general class of signals, which is the main contribution of this paper, and we apply this tool to Sparse FFT.
, we propose a new notion of isolation on average, which is more robust than the notion of isolation in buckets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
isolation on average, rather than isolation, is the right notion to use for analysing noisy hash schemes.
isolation on average can be a useful tool for analysing hashing schemes in settings where isolation is not sufficient to guarantee recovery, and that it can be useful in the context of Sparse FFT.

the notion of isolation in buckets is not a good tool for analysing noisy hash-based schemes in general, and we need a more robust notion that can capture the average behavior of a hash function in the presence of noise.
